Gantron College Football 2026

Updated Sun Oct 11, 9:40 AM CT
About the Model
100,000 simulated seasons per run from an ensemble of rating systems and market prices, with home-field advantage, every conference's official tiebreakers and the 12-team playoff bracket. Ratings are on a points scale: the gap between two teams is the expected margin on a neutral field. 1,029 Kalshi markets priced. Δwk compares with the Oct 4 run. Model version 0.28.120.
A few rating inputs haven't caught up on the Oct 10 games yet, so they sit out of the ratings until they do.

Rating = how many points better a team is than an average FBS team on a neutral field; tap a team for its card.

Column Guide
Win %each side's win chance - the away team on the left, the home team on the right - with a bar in the two teams' colors
Line / Our Linethe betting line and ours: the favorite and its number
DifferenceDiffours minus the line, in points; under More columns
Pickthe side we like at the betting line when ours differs by 2+ points (bold from 3)
Open Edgeour lean when the OPENER appeared - the first fresh line of the game's own week (Sun/Mon), not a preseason number - frozen at that moment; graded W/L/push once the game is final; under More columns
KickCentral time
Tap a gameratings and lines
Completedclosing line, our number, who covered
Power 4 / Group of 6 / conferenceonly games with a Power 4 team (ACC, B12, B1G, SEC), a Group-of-6 team, or a team from that conference on either side
Midweek / Sat Early / Afternoon / Nightthe time-slot buttons keep one slot: Midweek = every game not on a Saturday; Sat Early = Saturday kickoffs before 1:00 PM; Sat Afternoon = 1:00 PM to before 5:00 PM; Sat Night = 5:00 PM and later (Central); a game without a kickoff time yet shows under All only
Caveatleans at the market number, not edges

Each team's chance to reach and win its conference title game, from 100,000 simulated seasons, next to the Kalshi market's.

Column Guide
RatingRtgstrength in points
Projected Conf WinsxConfWexpected conference wins
Make Title GameApp%reach the title game
Win ConferenceWin%win the conference
Race bareach team's chance to win the conference as a slice of one bar in its colors; under it the likeliest title games and who wins them
MarketMkt%the market's chance: Kalshi price with the overround removed; each stays inside its own bid-ask, so a conference's market column need not add up to 100 when the market is overround
Fair OddsFairour fair odds
Edgeour edge after fees on the better side, in cents - Win = backing the team to win the conference, Not Win = betting against it (Make / Miss the title game on a division table)
Divisionsthe Sun Belt still plays in two divisions (East / West) and its title game is the two division winners: its card's Divisions switch shows each division's race and table - Win Division (Div%) = win the division, which is reaching the title game; Market and Edge from Kalshi's title-game markets

Filter
Column Guide
Betwhat has to happen for the bet to win - Over / Under a win line, Make / Miss the playoff, Win / Not Win a title. The price and our chance are for that outcome
Marketthe market's chance for that side (its Kalshi price), with American odds
Modelour chance for that side, with fair odds
Edge (¢)Edge¢model minus market after fees, in cents
Return (eROI)eROIexpected return: edge ÷ the price paid - the board's opening order, shaded green from 25%
Best Betstight, well-traded books, 20%+ eROI, 3¢+ edge after fees, priced 12% or higher (no long shots), and no team with fresh injury news (the line above the filters names any it holds back); Take = 2.5¢+ edge and 20%+ eROI with $200+ you can buy at the listed price; Maker = resting 1¢ inside the book still returns 30%+ with 3¢+ edge after the maker fee; Liquid = the busiest books; All = every market, no filters
Take $ / +2¢ $dollars you could buy on the bet side at the listed price, and paying up to 2¢ more (from the order book, before fees)
Taker / Makerwhose numbers the board shows. Taker = buying now at the listed price, after the taker fee. Maker = resting an order 1¢ inside the book, after its own (often lower) fee: Rest At is the price to post, Edge¢ and eROI what it earns if it fills - blank where the book is too wide to rest in. The Maker button switches to it, Best Bets and Take switch back
Advancedthe book (Bid / Ask), the Take $ columns and the volume
Heismanthe Heisman markets (Market = the player, Team = his school; or the winner's conference): Model = our Blend, the Heisman tab's number
Tiptap a team for its card; the search finds players too

Heisman projections57 candidates2% left for a winner outside the listStats and Kalshi prices Oct 11, 9:47 AM CT
Guide
# the Win % order - the table opens sorted by it
Player / Team his position beside his name; beside his team its rank in the Power Ratings (the PWR chip, 1 = the best team in FBS) and its record so far; click a team for its card
Proj Rec his team's projected regular-season record: expected wins - expected losses, to one decimal
QBR / EPA how efficient his season has been so far. A quarterback's Total QBR: a 0-100 grade of every play he makes - passing, running, sacks and fumbles - adjusted for the defenses faced (50 = average, 90+ = elite; Heisman-winning quarterbacks finished around 90). A back's or receiver's EPA per play: the expected points his plays added, not adjusted for the defense - receivers run higher than backs (a catch, not a carry), so each is colored against his own position. Hover for his percentile among FBS players of his position
Proj TD / Yds touchdowns and yards he is projected to be responsible for over the full season, title game included - passing, rushing and receiving together (the split on hover)
Base Score his Heisman Score in the base case - his average projected season - 0-100 with 50 = the average candidate here (most winners scored 98+ - Past Winners). It is graded against this week's candidates, so a Score moves when the others play, bye week or not. Win % can differ: it counts how often he finishes first across all simulated seasons, with the Kalshi price. Tap a player for what goes into it
Win % his projected chance to win the Heisman when ballots close (after the conference title games), with its American odds: our projection - the rest of the season simulated, and how Heisman voters have picked winners in the past - together with the Kalshi price. Part of the chance is left for a winner outside this list (the line above the table). One forecast among others, never a sure edge
Finalist his chance of being one of the four finalists invited to New York, with its American odds
Kalshi what a taker pays to buy YES right now - the ask plus Kalshi's fee - in cents (hover for bid / ask and the NO side)
Edge / eROI the better side for a taker now at his Win %, after fees: Win +4.9¢ = backing him to win (YES) is worth 4.9¢ more than it costs, Not Win = betting against him (NO); none = neither side pays. eROI = that edge over the price paid, shaded green from 25% (grey when neither side pays)
More columns adds his position, his team's record as a column of its own, its power rating (points better than an average FBS team on a neutral field), efficiency (passer rating for a quarterback, yards per touch for the rest), his team's projected losses and those against unranked teams, and American odds beside the Kalshi price. Show current stats adds the same stats so far, and the Score and win chance if the season ended today
Colors the stats are shaded against past Heisman finalists and winners when ballots closed: no color at an ordinary candidate's level, green from a lower finalist's level to full at a typical winner's (QBR against past quarterbacks; touchdowns, yards and efficiency against his position; team power, projected record and the rating; losses the other way), red below the average candidate; an unbeaten record shades green as the season goes on. The chances - Win %, Finalist and Curr % - are a different kind of number and shade violet instead (a violet line under their headers): a faint band down the column, darker the likelier (Win % full at 25%, the finalist chance from 20% to full at 75%). eROI shades green from 25%. Hover a column header for what it means
Tip click a player's row for his card - each stat now → projected at ballot time, bars for what he has banked of his projected touchdowns and yards, his Score and his chances (a small part of a total - a receiver's few carries - counts but is not listed); click a team for its card; click any column header to sort by it (again to reverse)
Base Score = his average (base-case) season · Win % = how often he finishes first across all simulated seasons, with the Kalshi price
